lines.text: I have been in a room with a living one, and I can assure you the mounted variety are a great improvement. It was in a hotel in Tangier. One does not forget a bedsheet with a tail on it.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Sam, you have the most appalling luck with hotels.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Rosalind, I have the most appalling luck with everything except you.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Darling, that is the nicest thing you have ever said, and you said it in front of a scorpion.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Anjali, you are not to put a hat on any of the caterpillars. I have asked politely.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: The Caterpillar Parade! Forty little velvet caterpillars, all marching in a line along a branch. I could eat them. I mean, I could dress them. In small hats.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: Please don't dress them in hats, Anjali.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Mark, they would be so happy.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: It is an excellent tableau. Notice that the leader has a little bite out of the leaf, and the others have not. The leader is always hungry.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: I believe that is true of every procession I have ever led, Professor.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Prudence, I should like to know why half the Archives is written in brown.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: The Oak Gall Basket! Little brown balls, each one a wasp's nursery, and each one the source of the finest ink in the world.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: Iron gall ink. It lasts for centuries. Half the Archives is written in it, and the other half is written in grief.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: You are very bleak this morning, Prudence.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: I am only accurate, Rosalind. It is a habit of the profession.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Is that why Ambrose's letters are brown and not black, Miss Quill?

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: Good heavens, Mr Pluck. Yes. It is. Whoever wrote them used a ten-year-old ink on a twenty-year-old page. Which means they were written last month.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Anjali, do not open that jar. It has been shut for twenty years, and the honey may be wise.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: The Beehive Honey Jar! Amber, thick, and still sweet after all this time. May I?

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Bose, it is an exhibit.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Cornelia, a jar of honey is not an exhibit until it has been used. It is merely a very expensive paperweight.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: A man's got to agree with her. The honey's warm, as well, you know. Somebody's kept the hive at the right temperature, in a room with no heating.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: That is not possible. Is it?

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: In this Hall, Mark, I have learned never to say that word.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: The Great Colony! Every ant, every bee, every wasp, in a glass nest the size of a wardrobe. And they're all, um, doing something useful.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Bloom, you are right. The Insectarium is restored, and for the first time in twenty years, every creature in this Hall has a job.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: I should like a job. Something dignified, with an ample budget.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Vane, you may sweep the Colony. The ants will supervise.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: A letter for you, Cornelia. It came by the morning post, in a heavy cream envelope. The seal is gilt, and the crest is a pair of golden scales.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Gilded League. Their offer is a kind one, which is the most dangerous kind. They wish to buy the Hall, and all that is in it, for a very handsome price.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: They have never stopped wanting it, Cornelia. I should know. I used to write their letters.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Thorne, this frame is so carefully pressed that I am afraid to breathe near it.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: The Pressed Flower Frame! Oh, my dears. Every petal in its place, every stem the colour of a good memory.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: It's the finest herbarium frame I've ever seen, Miss Thorne.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: It was a gift, Mark. From a man who could not tell a rose from a rutabaga, and who pressed this one for me anyway.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Ambrose.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: He was a dreadful gardener, Cornelia. And the only man I knew who could make a flower feel important. Do not tell the others.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: Mark, you have your eye pressed so hard to that microscope that you have left a ring on your face.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: The Pollen Microscope. Every grain a tiny jewel, every jewel a different shape.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: Look at this one, Miss Thorne. It looks like a spiked ball. And this one's a little crown.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Mark, you have the eye of a painter. You should hold a brush, not a trowel.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: I don't think I'm very good at, um, painting.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: No one is good at it until they have done it badly for ten years. Come to my studio on Thursday, and bring a very poor flower.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Mark, do not feed it anything with a pulse. I have seen what a pitcher plant can do.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: The Carnivorous Bog Jar! A little pitcher plant, with a lid like a tiny hat, and a puddle of something delicious at the bottom.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: I wouldn't put my finger in, Miss Bose.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: I have no intention of doing so. The recipe for pitcher-plant jelly is a closely guarded secret, and I mean to guard it very closely.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Do you know, I once saw a pitcher plant drown a bat? A very small bat. It did not look unhappy.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Professor, we do not need to know that.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Bose, there is a berry on your sleeve. And one on your hat. And, I think, one in your cup.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: The Coffee Tree! Real coffee. A whole branch of red berries, ripe and shining.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Mark! Give me that branch at once. I shall roast it, grind it, and make the finest cup of coffee in the history of the Society.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Bose, do not roast the exhibit.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Cornelia, I would never. I would take only the berries that fall.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: I've got a bowl, Miss Bose! They just fell. Two dozen of them. All at once.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: Miss Thorne, I think it's, um, singing. A little bit. If you stand underneath.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: The Seed Pod Mobile! A hundred seed pods, dangling from fine brass wires, and turning in the draught.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: You may hear them rattle if you walk beneath. Each one a different note.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: It's a wind chime made of pods. I'd never have thought of that.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Hugo, you'd never have thought of it because it is not a machine. It is simply beautiful, and does nothing at all.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: I'll have you know, Rosalind, I've started to appreciate things that do nothing at all. It's the best thing about this place.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: Rosalind, the page at the back is blank, and the flower beside it has no name. Do you know it?

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: The Great Botanical Atlas. Every plant the Society ever collected, drawn and named. Half of it is mine, the other half is the work of the Hall itself.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: There's a page near the back that is blank, with a title: Unrecorded. And, um, a little pressed flower that I don't recognise.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Mark, show me. Dear God. It is a flower that has never grown in any garden I have visited.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: It is a flower from the edge of the map, Rosalind. I brought a seed home, years ago. I gave it to the founder, and I did not ask why.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Then he planted it somewhere in this Hall. We must find the plant.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Bose, are these pills, or are they sweets? I should hate to make a mistake.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: The Pill Tile. Small, round, grey, and very much in need of a spoonful of sugar. I remember this tile from the ship.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: Did people really take these?

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Every day, and with great ceremony, Mark. Then they were sick, and I fed them broth, and they took another.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: I was once cured of a cough by one of these. Or I was cured of the cough by the horror of taking it. Hard to say.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Apothecary Annex is open, then. Professor, you will go first.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: Aldous, why is the jar rocking? Is it the leeches, or is it you?

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: The Leech Jar. Do you know, I had a very odd feeling just now. As though the jar were looking at me.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: It's the leeches, Professor. They look at everyone. It's the whole point of them.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: I consulted a leech once, in Lyons. He was most reassuring. Told me I was in perfect health, apart from a degree of moral decay.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: It is a very distinguished leech, Mr Vane, if it can diagnose the Society's patron at a distance.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Do give him my regards, Sam. I should like to know what he thinks of me.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Anjali, tell me honestly. Is this cup for washing the eye, or for drinking from?

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: The Eye Bath Cups! Tiny glass cups, with a lip shaped to fit around the eye. A wonderfully peculiar invention.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: I tried one, Miss Bose. It's quite refreshing. Like having a very small cold bath in the face.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Then you will tell me whether it works, Barnaby. I do not have the stomach for it.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: Does it work, Barnaby?

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: I don't know. I can see an awful lot of tiny stars, though. All the way up to the top of the Dome.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: It is working very well, Mr Pluck. You are seeing things that were not previously visible.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Mark, my dear, you must put the rosemary at the front, where everybody can reach it.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: The Herb Jar Shelf. Rosemary, thyme, sage, and a very old jar labelled Remembrance. I think it's just rosemary.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: It is just rosemary, Mark. The name was a little joke between Ambrose and me. He said it was for the days when the Hall forgot itself.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: That is why it has a place at the front of the shelf, I suppose.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: Can I grow some? In the Conservatory. For, um, remembering.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Bloom, you may grow as much remembrance as you like. It is one of the few things the Hall is short of.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Miss Quill, is my name in the ledger? I'd rather like to know what I'm prescribed.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: The Remedy Ledger Stand. Every patient, every ailment, every prescription, in the hand of the apothecary. It is a meticulous document.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Prudence, is there any mention of a bird in it? I think I may have been prescribed a bird at some stage.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: Professor, there is no such remedy as a bird. There is, however, a prescription for you on page nine, and it says: rest, tea, and fewer swifts.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: There is another entry. Dated the eve of his vanishing. A. Hall: one draught, to be taken at the clock. Not to be repeated.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: Which clock, Cornelia? That is the question.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Spirit Lamp. A little blue flame in a glass cup. I could cook a very small egg on it.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Oh, I could do a great deal better than an egg, Hugo. Hand it over.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: I'll polish it for you, Anjali. You'll never see a flame so true.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Why do they call it a spirit lamp, Miss Wren? Are there spirits in it?

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: It burns spirits of wine, Mr Pluck. Not those sort of spirits. We are far too well bred for that.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Zephyrine, this smells of roses, and of something older. What is it?

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: The Dragon's Blood Jar. A resin the colour of dried roses, and as sweet as incense. It comes from a tree on an island that is not on any chart.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Then how do you know where it is, Zephyrine?

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: Because I have been there. It is shaped like a thumb, and it smells of vanilla, and the natives are the politest people in the world.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: I should like to see it. When the Hall is finished, I mean to take a holiday.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Miss Wren! You said holiday! Can I write that on my cuff?

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Hugo, someone has been ringing that bell all morning. I cannot find the person.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: The Chemist's Counter Bell! One ding, and a very sleepy apothecary comes shuffling out of the back.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Pluck, there is no apothecary.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: I know, Miss Wren. But I've been ringing it all morning, and every time, a bottle moves.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: A bottle moves.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Yes, Professor! A very small one, three inches to the left. It's trying to help.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Then we shall see to it that it gets a very good review.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Sulphur Block. Bright yellow, and it smells of a match gone wrong. I'd keep it well away from the music box.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Hugo, you have the most sensible instincts. A pity so few of them are applied to the people around you.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Ha! I'll take that as a compliment, Sam, and I'll try to find a polite way to kick you out of the room.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Is it safe, Hugo? Because I wish to make a lemon tart in the Annex, and I will need the Spirit Lamp.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: It's safe, Anjali, as long as nobody lights a match in the vicinity of the block. Or of Sam.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Hugo, do these tubes hold anything that might spoil a soup? I should like to be told.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: The Test Tube Rack. Thirty glass tubes, each labelled with a letter, and each containing a drop of coloured water.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: The letters, Professor. Read them in order.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: A, N, D, R, E... no, it is: R, E, M, E, M, B, E, R. Remember. Over and over, in a ring.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Whoever set this out wanted us to see it, and wanted us to read it. Remember what?

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: It is not an instruction, Cornelia. It is a plea.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Sam, if you think that pot can turn lead into gold, I should like a word with you before you try it.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Philosopher's Crucible. A little pot of black iron, with a handle shaped like a serpent. It's said to turn lead into gold, though I have yet to see it do a thing.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Hugo, if it could, I would have it in my pocket by now.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: You would not know what to do with a pocketful of gold, Sam. You would spend it by Thursday, and borrow more by Friday.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: That is a very good description of my entire career, Rosalind. And a very accurate one.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: I would put a few coins in it, to see what happened. For science. And for fun.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: The Dragon Scale Salve! A pot of thick green cream that smells of mint and thunderstorms. I made it for the sailors, when they had blisters.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: It's, um, surprisingly effective, Anjali. I tried it on my thumb.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Of course it is. I developed it on the longest voyage the Society ever mounted. Never mind the dragon. It is mostly lard, mint, and good cheer.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: It is the finest thing in the Annex, then. You will take a jar to every member of the Society.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: All of them? Cornelia, there are four hundred and sixty-two.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: I am quite certain, Miss Bose, that you can manage.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Quill, does the Pharmacopoeia mention a cure for curiosity? I fear we all have it.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: The Grand Pharmacopoeia. All of it, from aconite to zinc. Seven hundred pages, bound in green cloth, with the founder's own annotations in the margins.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Splendid! And is there any remedy for forgetfulness?

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: There is. Page four hundred and twelve. It says: Seek the thing you have lost, where you last put it down. A very sensible prescription.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: There is a note under it, in the founder's hand. And where did I put it down, I wonder? In the one place I never look.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: That is the oldest trick in the book, Cornelia. He hid it in plain sight.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: The Annex is restored, my dears. Now, come and let us see the gems. I confess I have missed them dreadfully.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: Rosalind, you are holding that ring as though it might bite. Whose was it?

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: The Ring Cushion! A hundred little rings, each in its own velvet hollow. I recognise nearly every one.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Rosalind, I do believe you recognise some of them from your own hand.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Sam, if you have been looking at my hand, I shall ask you to return what you took from it.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: I took nothing, I swear! I only admired. Once. In 1887.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: I suggest we move on, before Mr Vane is forced to confess to anything further.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Sam, you are standing at that case far too casually. What have you got in your pocket?

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: The Opal Heart Case. A single stone, the size of a hen's egg, with a fire in it that moves.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Cornelia, I must tell you something. When I came to this Hall I meant to take this. I came with a very good plan, and a very small chisel.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: I know, Mr Vane. I have known for some time.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: You knew?

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Pluck followed you on your first night. He has been carrying your chisel in his apron pocket ever since.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: It's a very good chisel, Mr Vane! I've been keeping it sharp.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Rosalind, I do believe that necklace is winking at me.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: The Crown Jewels of the Society! The tiara, the necklace, the little silver ring I wore when I became patroness. They are all here, all clean, and all in their places.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: And not a single one in my pocket, Cornelia. I should like it noted in the minutes.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: It shall be noted, Mr Vane. Under the heading of Remarkable Events.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Dear Sam. You have grown. One notices it in the way you stand, a little further from the exit.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Rosalind, I have been looking for that exit for twenty years. I find I do not much mind not finding it.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: We should have a party, Miss Wren! A proper one, with jelly!

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Zephyrine, I have been looking at that jar for five minutes. What exactly is in it?

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: The Cosmic Dust Jar! A thimbleful of the sky, collected from the roof of a cathedral in Prague. I wonder what it dreamed of, before it fell.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: A small, grey, unambitious dream, I should think. Of being a very large star.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: It's the last grain of a star, that, Professor. And it's going to sit very nicely next to my best pair of tweezers.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Meteorite Chamber is open. Mr Pemberton, do not touch anything that is warm.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Cornelia, everything in this room is warm.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Rosalind, do not wear those beads in the dark. They have a very odd glint.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: The Tektite Beads. Small black beads of glass, formed in the moment a meteorite hits the ground. Every one a tiny scar from the sky.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: They would make a very fine necklace.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: I made one once, for the king of a small island. He wore it every day, and said it brought him good fortune.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: And what became of the king?

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: He lost his island in a game of cards. But he kept the necklace, and said it was a good bargain.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Pemberton, is it true that rock came from the moon? I should like to see the paperwork.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: The Moon Rock Case! A genuine sliver of the moon, brought down by the Society's own expedition.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: How did they get it, Professor? Did they go up in a balloon?

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: They did not, Barnaby. The moon dropped it, on a Tuesday, in a field in Kent. A farmer noticed it, and was very upset about his turnips.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Professor, that is not what the label says.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: The label has been tidied up, Cornelia. For the visitors.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Shooting Star Mobile! A cluster of silver stars, each one on a little spring, so they sway and twinkle in the air.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: It's the best thing in the room, Hugo!

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: It's only a mobile, Barnaby. But I'll admit, every time it moves, I feel it in my chest. As if somebody had finally got the timing right.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: It is a very calming effect. I recommend it to anyone who has been rearranging Archives for eight weeks.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: I've been standing underneath it for ten minutes. I don't think I want to move.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Zephyrine, a mile of rock, and a message at the bottom. Who on earth wrote it?

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: The Planet Core Sample. A cylinder of rock, drawn from a hole a mile deep. At the very bottom, a layer of something that does not belong to the rest.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: What is it, Zephyrine?

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: I do not know, Rosalind. The assayer said it was a very old kind of metal. The founder said it was a message. I did not like to ask which of them was right.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: If it is a message, Miss Blackwood, who is it from?

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: From the bottom of the world. Or, perhaps, from a man who wished to be taken for a very old kind of metal. I shall let you know when I find out.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Hugo, tap it again. Gently. I believe it said something that sounded like my name.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Impact Glass Vase! A shape like a tulip, formed from sand that got hit by a falling rock. It rings when you tap it. A very pure E-flat.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Oh, let me. It would make a lovely sound for a dinner bell.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Anjali, you tap it, and I'll tell you precisely which pitch it is.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: E-flat, Hugo?

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: You're a natural, Anjali. You tapped it exactly in the middle, as if you'd done it all your life.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: I have done it all my life. With a spoon, on a great many pots.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: The Skyfall Altar! A great slab of black stone, on which the largest meteorite in the Society's collection rests, like a cat on a cushion.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Meteorite Chamber is whole. It has taken three weeks, and I have not had a decent cup of tea since the second.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Cornelia, I made you a cup this morning. It is on your desk.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Bose. When?

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: At eight o'clock. I left it on the blotter, beside the card that says Wednesday.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: There is no cup, Miss Bose. And the card has been in the drawer for months.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: The Whispering Shell. Miss Wren, if I hold it to my ear, I can hear somebody talking. But it's very faint.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: What does it say, Mr Pluck?

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: It says your name. And then it says: Not yet.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: That is the same phrase Zephyrine found on her chart. Tell Cornelia. Not yet.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Whoever is saying it knows precisely what we are doing, and wishes us to continue. I find that more reassuring than I ought.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Quill, has anyone told the lift that it is not meant to carry letters?

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: The Dumbwaiter of Secrets. A small lift in the wall of the Cabinet, which was used for passing notes between the curators.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: It's in perfect working order, Miss Quill! It goes up and down, and nobody falls out!

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: It also has a secret compartment, which I have just opened. Inside, a single folded letter.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Read it aloud, please.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: It says: Dear Cornelia, if you are reading this, you are further than I expected. I am proud of you. Do not trust the League. And have a biscuit.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: He wrote that. In his own hand. And somehow, I believe that was the last biscuit in the Hall.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: The Silent Bell! It's got no clapper, Miss Wren, so it just hangs there and doesn't ring. I like him. He's sensible.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: It does ring, Barnaby. It rings at a pitch too low to hear, and it makes the floor hum. Put your hand on the wall.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Oh! It's like a purr. A very large, very distant purr.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: I believe it is a call, rather than a bell. Something is meant to hear it, and I should rather like to know what.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: The same something that stands by the third griffin, Professor. Sam and I found the door last night.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: You found the door, Miss Blackwood? And you did not wake me?

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Zephyrine, I put my ear to that horn, and I could hear someone breathing. It was not me.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: The Great Whisper. A tall brass horn, curled like a shell, that gathers every murmur in the Hall and sends it back from a single point.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: And what does it say, now that it is restored?

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: It says, Cornelia, in a very quiet voice: the third griffin turns left.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: And the door behind the third griffin leads to a little spiral stair, and the stair leads to a very old door with a very old lock. It is the Founder's Study, I am quite certain.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Study is real, then. And we cannot open it until the Hall is ready.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: It is real, Cornelia. I have been through that door, once, long ago. When the time comes, I shall go in with you, if you will have me.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Cornelia, the lamp lit itself as I passed. I felt rather flattered.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: The Stair Newel Lamp! It's the first one that lights itself when you walk past. Look, Miss Wren, it says hello!

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: That is a very polite lamp. The Portrait Stair has an excellent standard of hospitality.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: It's got a photoelectric cell, Barnaby. Well. A very early one. I'd say it was Ambrose's own design.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: A fine device. And I observe that it lights only for members of the Society. It did not light for the League's man, last week.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Did you stand on the stair that day, Miss Quill?

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: I did. In my best boots. It was extremely satisfying.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Thorne, kindly explain why the Duchess has a peacock on her head.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: The Duchess of Peacocks! My dears, I painted her myself. She was a very formidable woman, and she paid in peacocks.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: How many peacocks, Rosalind?

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Six. Of whom four were very bad-tempered, and two were exquisite. I kept the two.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: She's got a peacock on her hat, Miss Thorne, and a peacock on her shawl, and a peacock on her parasol.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: She was devoted to them, Barnaby. When she died, she left the Society a single feather, and a note: Remember me by my worst habit.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Cornelia, how long has that frame been empty? And whom was it meant for?

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Empty Frame. A great gilt frame, with nothing in it, hanging at the turn of the stair.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: It has been empty for twenty years, Cornelia. It was meant for a portrait of the Society's founding members, painted together. We never found the time to sit.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: I shall sit, Rosalind. I shall sit all day, if it is any help. I believe I shall not need to move.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: You would have to be moved, Aldous. Like a very handsome lump of granite.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Then we shall fill it, all of us. In good time. When we have finished the rest.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Miss Wren, there's a little brass tag on the corner. It says: Reserved. A.H.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Rosalind, I would swear that portrait is about to say something rude.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: The Founder's Great Portrait. Oh, I remember painting this. He would not sit still, and so the whole canvas is a little blurred about the edges.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: He looks as though he is about to speak.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: He was always about to speak. It was his chief fault, and his greatest charm. Look at the eyes. I painted them last, at three in the morning, and he said they were the first honest likeness of him.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: The eyes are looking at the wall to his left, Rosalind. The wall where the Founders' Gallery begins.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Then that is where we shall go next. Let us see what Ambrose wished to show us.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Cornelia, whose hat is that? I should like to have a word with him.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Founder's Hat Stand. A dark oak post, with three brass hooks and, upon the highest, a single top hat. It is dusty, and very slightly warm.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: It's still got the shape of his head in it, Miss Wren! Look!

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: Leave it where it hangs, Mr Pluck. It is the only object in the Hall which has never been moved, and it is a great comfort to the Archives.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: It is rather like seeing a man's ghost, but only from the back.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: I have a very strong urge to lift it off and look inside. I do not, I am happy to say, have the nerve.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Neither have I, Professor. I mean to keep it on its hook until the man himself returns to collect it.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Prudence, the Charter is in nine inks. Any idea who ran out of black?

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: The Founding Charter Frame. The original Charter of the Curio Society, signed by nine members, in nine different inks.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Only eight signatures are legible, Miss Quill.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: The ninth has faded. It is Ambrose's. And beneath it, in a very different ink, a line that has been added: Revised. By A. H. The day he vanished.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Somebody went into the Founders' Gallery on the last day, then, and changed the Charter.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: Not changed it. Added to it. A new clause, at the very bottom, in letters so small that it needs a magnifying glass. I have the glass.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: What does the clause say, Prudence?

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: It says: Should the Hall fall silent, the Society shall be re-formed by whoever opens the doors.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Sam, you look as though you are sitting in a church pew. Relax.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Founder's Writing Desk. The very desk at which he wrote the Charter, and all the great letters to the Society. Mahogany, with a green leather top.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: May I sit? Just for a moment, Cornelia. I have wanted to sit in that chair for twenty years.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: You may sit, Mr Vane. But you may not open the drawers.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: I would not dream of it. I have spent half my life trying to open this man's drawers, and I would like, for once, to try being polite.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: There's a note under the blotter, Mr Vane! Look!

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: It is addressed to me. It says: Sam, you were right about the monarchs. Go and apologise to Rosalind.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Oh, how very like him. He never could resist having the last word.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Pemberton, the skylight is leaking light. Kindly stop it at once.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Gallery Skylight Lantern! A great glass cage with a hundred little panes, and in the middle a lamp that lights the whole Gallery from above.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: A splendid piece, Hugo, and the light, my goodness, it is exactly the colour of a barn owl's breast.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: It'll want a bit of wire, a spot of oil, and a very fine chain. I'll make it good as new.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Pemberton, you could not make a thing worse if you tried.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: That's the nicest thing anyone's ever said to me, Cornelia. I'll put it on a card.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: I'll write it on my cuff.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Prudence, who would tear pages from a diary? And why so neatly?

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: The Founder's Diary Stand. An oak lectern, with a leather diary open at a page in the middle of the last winter. The pages afterwards have been cut out.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The cuts are the same as the ones in the Folio. A single sharp blade, and a very steady hand.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: I have compared the cuts, Cornelia. They match, but not in any way that I can explain. They are, in fact, too clean. They were made by a blade that is very old, and was sharpened yesterday.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: I know someone who sharpens old blades. A cartographer called Rook. I will find him.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Zephyrine, take Sam. He may be of use, for once.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Rosalind, my dear, I have always been of use. It is merely that the use was not always lawful.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Hugo, if that needle is sharp, kindly do not put it near a bird.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Founder's Gramophone! A brass horn the size of a lily, a wax cylinder, and a needle that's been sharpened by someone who knew what they were doing.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Will it play, Mr Pemberton?

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: It plays, Cornelia. But it's not a recording of anyone's voice. It's a very slow, quiet rhythm. Tick. Pause. Tick. Tick. Pause.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: That is a code, surely.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: Morse. Slowed by a factor of ten. And it is saying: WEDNESDAY. NOON. THE CLOCK TOWER.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Clock Tower. That is wing forty-six, Miss Quill. We are a long way off.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Miss Wren, it's a Wednesday today.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: Cornelia, the fire has just lit itself. Did you do it?

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Founding Fire. The great hearth of the Gallery, which has stood cold for twenty years, and which I have just lit.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Oh, Cornelia. It is the loveliest thing I have seen since I came back. Do you hear the fire? It is singing.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: The whole Society is here. All of us, together, in front of the founding fire. I believe it is the first time since the winter he vanished.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Cornelia, I should like to say, in front of all these people, that I came to the Hall to steal it, and I will stay to guard it.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Vane, that is the nicest thing you have said in thirty years. The Society, as of this evening, has a quorum.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Three cheers for Miss Wren!

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Thorne, I believe the palm is looking at me. Do tell it to stop.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: The Parlour Palm. A great spray of green fronds in a brass pot, to shade the music boxes from the afternoon sun.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: It's in, um, rather good health. I think it was waiting for somebody to talk to it.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Everyone is, Mark. Talk to it for ten minutes a day, and it will outlive us all.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: In the Tea Room, we talk to the dough. It works exactly the same way.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: I talk to Hannibal, Miss Bose. He's an excellent listener. He never interrupts.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: Hugo, it plays a different tune each time, doesn't it? Even when you wind it the same.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Carousel Music Box! A little merry-go-round of painted horses, turning on a brass spindle, and playing a waltz in a very sweet tin voice.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Can I wind it, Hugo?

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Gently, Barnaby. Three turns, no more. You don't want to tell it how you're feeling.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Oh! It plays a different tune each time, Hugo!

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: It plays the tune that wants to be played. I've never seen a box that did that before, and I'd like to know who put the idea in it.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Quill, the dancer has stopped turning. Is she waiting for something?

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: The Dancing Doll Box. The lid opens, a little porcelain dancer rises, and she turns on one toe to a very delicate melody.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: She is exquisite. I painted her portrait once, in watercolour. She was the only sitter I have ever had who did not complain.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: Each of her movements corresponds to a point on a compass. I should say she is also a chart, and I should say that she is pointing at the Clock Tower.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Then everything is pointing at the Clock Tower, Miss Blackwood.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: Everything but the pigeons, Cornelia. They have their own agenda.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: Hugo, the sixth note is back, and something has clicked in the wall. Do not touch anything.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Great Music Box. Seven hundred pins, and I've mended every one. Cornelia, would you like to hear what it plays?

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Pemberton, I would.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: It's the lullaby. All of it, with the sixth note put back. And listen. When the sixth note sounds, something in the wall clicks.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: A panel has opened, behind the pipes. There is a stack of pages inside. Cut pages. Pages from the Folio, and from the diary.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: Every one of them. In order. It will take me a week to read them, and I will not sleep.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Then I shall send up a very large pot of tea, Miss Quill. And a great many biscuits.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Prudence, I once attended a Concert for Seventeen Triangles. It was extremely difficult to follow.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: The Drying Line. A row of damp prints hanging from a cord, each one a poster for a Society lecture of long ago. A Talk on Larks. A Debate on the Moon.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: A Concert for Seventeen Triangles! Who on earth went to that, Miss Quill?

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: Seventeen triangles went, Mr Pluck. And they were, I am told, a great success.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: I attended a lecture on Moths, in this very Hall, with a young woman who has since become an exacting archivist.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: Mr Vane, you were not at that lecture. I would have remembered.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Prudence, I was in the back row. I was the one who laughed at the wrong place.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Thorne, I believe someone has been using the blue ink. There is a smear on the doorknob.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: The Colour Ink Cans! Every shade of the rainbow, in a row of brass-lidded pots. I could paint the whole Hall.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: Miss Thorne, I painted something this week. It's not very good.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Show me, Mark. Do. Oh, my dear, this is a snail. It is a very good snail, and it has a most interesting look about the eye.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: It's a snail with a hat. I thought, um, everything's better with a hat.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Mark Bloom. You have a gift. You must paint a hundred more.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Prudence, what is the use of an engraving bench if nobody will engrave on it?

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: The Engraving Bench. A copper plate, a burin, and a little brass magnifier. I find that I am rather fond of it.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Quill, you are smiling.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: It is a very good bench, Cornelia. It reminds me that it is possible to make a mark that lasts for a hundred years, if one is patient and does not tremble.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Prudence, I do believe you are the only person I know who thinks of patience as a pleasure.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: I think of patience as a form of revenge, Aldous. It is a good deal more satisfying.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Pemberton, I believe you have lead on your chin.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Typecaster! A little brass furnace, and a mould for casting a letter at a time. It pops out a perfect A every three seconds.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: I can make a whole alphabet, Hugo!

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: You can, and I'll help. Careful with the hot lead. We'll make you a set of your own. One for each of your good remarks.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: A whole fount, Hugo! A fount of wisdom!

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Pluck, I do not believe that is what the word means. But I shall allow it.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Quill, are these the same invitations we sent last Tuesday, or are they new ones?

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: The Printing Revolution. A great iron press, operated by a crank, and still wet with a fresh black ink I cannot account for.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Has someone been printing, Miss Quill?

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: The first sheet is on the tray. It reads: The Curio Society invites its members, living, lapsed, and long forgotten, to return to the Hall. Signed: C. Wren, Curator. I did not write it.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Nor did I. But it is a very handsome sheet, Cornelia. And I rather think we should send it.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Pluck, you will take it to the post. All four hundred and sixty-two copies.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Aye, Miss Wren! I shall need a very large bag.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Anjali, you've got flour on the glue pot. Please stop that.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: The Glue Pot! A little iron pot, always simmering, and always smelling of horse. Miss Wren, I've stuck three things to my sleeve already.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Do stop sticking things to your sleeve, Mr Pluck.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: You've got to wait for the glue to set, Barnaby. It's a patient craft, shipbuilding. The only way to hurry it is to do it twice.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: I make a very good glue from flour and water. And I have never once stuck anything to my sleeve.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Miss Bose, you have glue on your sleeve now.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: That, Barnaby, is a béchamel. It is a very different thing.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Pemberton, I should like to know how a mast gets round, and who turns it.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Mast Maker's Lathe! A great round of oak turning slowly, and a long ribbon of shavings curling off the tool.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: Every mast is a promise, Hugo. A promise that the ship will come home.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: They don't always, Zephyrine.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: No. But the masts are always straight. That is the part that is under our control.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: I should like that on the wall of the Curator's Office, Miss Blackwood. Every mast is a promise.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: I'll write it on a card, Miss Wren.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: The Schooner Model! Three masts, forty sails, a little bronze figurehead of a woman with her hair blowing back. She is the Wanderer. I sailed in her.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Blackwood, you sailed in a model?

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: I sailed in the ship she was copied from. And the ship, in turn, sailed in Ambrose's wake. He led us to the edge of the chart, and then, rather cheerfully, vanished over it.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: He left a note in the galley, as I recall. It said: Back by Wednesday. We were there for eleven months.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: I do think it is wonderful that he is consistent.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Hugo, may I climb up the crane? I should like to see the Hall from above.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Dock Crane! A little iron jib on a rotating base, with a hook the size of my thumb, and a chain that clinks like loose change.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: I can lift a mouse with it, Hugo! A real one!

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: You may lift one, Barnaby. Not for long. And with its permission.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: He says it's fine, Hugo. He says it's the best ride he's ever had.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: A mouse lifted by a crane! I believe it is the highest altitude achieved by any member of the family since the last owl.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Quill, there is a ship in the ledger that did not return. Who was her captain?

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: The Harbour Master's Desk. Every ship that has ever left this Hall's imagination is recorded here, in a fat ledger. Date, cargo, port of call.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Is there a ship that never returned?

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: There is one. The last entry, dated twenty years ago. The ship's name is Meridian. The cargo is blank, and the port of call is blank. And the Master has written, in the margin: Do not wait for her.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: The Meridian. I know that name. I saw her once, off the southern edge, sailing with all her lamps lit, and no one on deck.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Blackwood, you did not tell us.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: I am telling you now, Cornelia. I did not wish to say it until I was sure that I believed it.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Hugo, the little clock is a quarter of an hour fast. And the big one is in agreement with it.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Chronometer Box. Two gimbals, a brass-bound case, and a very fine clock that keeps time to a fraction of a second. I haven't heard a better.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: A chronometer is a cartographer's best friend. It tells you where you are, by telling you what time it is somewhere else.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: A rather philosophical proposition, Zephyrine.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: All good navigation is, Aldous. The world is simple if you know when it is.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: And do we know when it is, Mr Pemberton?

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: It's six minutes past four, Cornelia. And according to this, exactly six minutes past four in a place I haven't heard of.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: Barnaby, you are leaning on the rail. I should hate to have to catch you.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: The Gallery Anchor Rope Rail! Real rope, tarred and knotted, with a great brass anchor at the end. It smells wonderfully of ships.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: It smells of tar, Mr Pluck.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: That's the same thing, Miss Wren. In a good way.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: I rather like a ship's rail. One feels, leaning on it, as though one were about to say something important, and be believed.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: That is the effect of the sea, Sam. Not of the rail.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Rosalind, it is the effect of the rail, as well. I have tested it.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Hugo, is the ironclad really the size of my kitchen table? I had no idea.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Ironclad Model! A grey, rivetted, ridiculous thing, and utterly magnificent. Every plate is the size of a stamp.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Does it have guns, Hugo?

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Eight, Barnaby. They fire little peas, if you load them right.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Peas! I'll bring a bag.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Bose, if there is a pea battle in the Model Ship Hall, I shall resign.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Cornelia, a good commander never resigns. She merely redeploys the peas.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Zephyrine, a hundred ships on a floor. And a space for one more. I wonder who is expected.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Great Armada. A hundred ships, in a hundred sizes, drawn up in a long crescent across the floor of the Hall. It is the grandest thing we have restored.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: There is one model missing, Cornelia. At the very centre of the crescent, there is a little round hole, and a brass tag. It says: Meridian.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Maybe somebody took her for a bath, Miss Wren.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Nobody took her. She has not come home. And I have a feeling the Balloon Loft is going to tell us why.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: I shall bring the binoculars. And a very large bird book.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Barnaby, you have been weaving that for an hour. May I know what it is?

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: The Basket Maker's Bench! A pile of cane, a little knife, and a half-woven basket that looks exactly like a hat.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: It is a basket, Mr Pluck.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: It's a hat, Miss Wren. I've tried it on. It's a very good hat, and it fits me perfectly.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: I will fill your hat with sandwiches, Barnaby. It will be the first hat in history to be eaten from.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: I wove one, too. It's, um, got a handle. I think it's a bag.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: It is a bag, Mark. A very distinguished one. Don't let anybody tell you otherwise.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: Hugo, I do not wish to alarm anyone, but that flame is blue.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Hot Air Burner! A fine brass nozzle, a fuel line, and a cone of blue flame that roars like a lion.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Splendid! It is the sound a heron makes, when disturbed at dinner.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: I'll take your word for it, Professor. Mind your eyebrows.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: I recommend a very large bucket of water, within reach. And a copy of the Fire Regulations.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Quill, you are always so reassuringly pessimistic.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: It is the only form of optimism that has ever kept a library intact, Cornelia.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: If nobody is looking, Mr Pemberton, I should like a short ride on the cart.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Launch Cart! A little wooden dolly on iron wheels, to carry a basket to the launch deck. It rolls like a dream.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Can I ride in it, Hugo?

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Not on your own, Barnaby. Not until we've tested the brakes.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: What if I put Hannibal in it, instead?

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Hannibal's an umbrella stand. He's built for a dignified life of standing still.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Hannibal says he's ready to travel, Hugo.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Aldous, the gauge has dropped a full inch in the last quarter of an hour.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Air Pressure Gauge. A big brass dial, with a needle that swings between Storm and Fair. I'm telling you now, it's dropping like a stone.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: That is not a good sign, if we are about to launch.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Ha! A storm! Then we shall see the swifts come in. They always know, you see, a good hour before the weather does.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Professor, the swifts are not here.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Cornelia, you are right. They should be, and they are not. I do not like it.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Hugo, if you put the Professor in that thing, I shall write to his mother.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: The Ornithopter! A flying machine with wings of silk and bamboo, and a little steam engine in the middle. It has never flown, you know. Not once.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: It will, Professor. I've been working on it. A few tweaks to the pivot, a few changes to the flap, and I'd say she's ready for a very short hop.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: You are going to fly it, Hugo?

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: No. I'm going to give it to you.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Me? Oh. Oh, no. I am a bird watcher, not a bird. I am only qualified to look up.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: A short hop, Professor. Mr Pluck will hold the rope.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Zephyrine, how high does a balloon go before it stops being a balloon?

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: The Great Altitude Record Balloon. Forty feet of silk, painted with a map of the stars. It rose higher than any balloon in history, and came down in a very surprised sheep field.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: How high, Miss Blackwood?

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: Higher than the clouds, Barnaby. High enough that the pilot could see the edge of the sea, and a little way beyond it.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Who was the pilot?

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: The Society's founder. He did it alone, in the summer before he vanished. He came down at midnight, and said only: there is a great deal more of it.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Barnaby, nobody has touched that bell! It rang all on its own!

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Launch Deck Bell. A bronze bell, hung from a post at the edge of the deck, to signal the departure of every balloon.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: I'll ring it, Miss Wren!

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: You will ring it when we are ready, Mr Pluck. And not a moment before.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: I'll just touch it. Lightly. To see how it feels.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Barnaby, don't!

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Oh. It rang. Hugo, it rang by itself! I never even touched it!

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Barnaby, are the baskets loaded? Mr Pemberton, is the burner lit? Professor, are the invitations tied?

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Great Balloon Launch. Every member of the Society is here, on the deck, in the evening sun. And the balloon is rising.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: There she goes! Oh, how splendid! She is carrying the invitations, you know. Four hundred and sixty-two of them, tied to the basket.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: It's the best thing I've ever seen, Miss Wren. It's like a very large, very slow, very polite bird.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Cornelia, the sky has gone the colour of a good brandy. I think it is a very good omen.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: I do not trust omens. But I have, on occasion, been persuaded by the weather.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Balloon Loft is restored. And the Society is calling. Let us see who answers.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: The Stargazer's Planter! A big stone trough, full of moonflowers that only open at night. Um, I've been waiting for it to bloom.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Mark, it has. Look. Every flower is turned up to the sky, as if it were listening.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: They're, um, very white. They look like small lamps, on long green stalks.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: I should like to paint them, Rosalind. In silver, on a blue-black ground.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: We shall paint them together, Zephyrine. You will provide the stars, and I will provide the stems.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: Professor, there's a, um, wren in the bath! A little one, with a very serious look.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: The Bird Bath! A shallow stone basin, with a little brass fountain in the middle. And, oh, look, Cornelia. A wren, bathing in the shallow end!

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Professor, I should like you to explain what that means.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: It means, my dear Cornelia, that the Observatory Walk is, as far as the birds are concerned, open for business.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Three robins, a blackbird, and a thrush! They've all come at once!

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: It is the first rule of birdwatching, Barnaby. Provide a bath, and everything else will follow.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Sam, you have been sitting in that chair for an hour, and I do not believe you have watched a single cloud.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: The Cloud Watcher's Chair. A deep wicker seat, with a footstool and a blanket. A chair in which one does absolutely nothing at all.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Rosalind, I would be a magnificent cloud watcher. I have a great deal of experience in doing absolutely nothing.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: You do not, Sam. You are the busiest idler in the Society. You merely take your holidays in other people's pockets.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Do you know, I believe you are right. I think I have been busy doing nothing for thirty years, and it has been exhausting.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Sit down, Mr Vane. Watch a cloud. It will do you good.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: Hugo, the strings are humming. Do you hear it? It is the sixth note, a little flat.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Wind Harp! A set of brass strings, strung across a frame, and played by the breeze. Hear it? Every gust is a chord.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: It is playing the lullaby. Slowly, and slightly flat.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: It's playing it a little wrong, Zephyrine. Look, the sixth string's loose.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: Tighten it, Hugo. And let us hear what happens when it is right.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The lullaby, in the open air, over the Observatory Walk. It sounds like the Hall itself is humming.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Cornelia, I climbed all the way up, and the whole Hall is lit beneath me like a jewel box.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Watchers' Lantern. A tall brass lamp on a stone post, at the end of the Walk. It stands at the highest point of the Hall, and its light can be seen for miles.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: The record says it was lit every night, for forty years, by whoever was on watch. The last entry is the night of the founder's disappearance.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Then we shall light it, and keep it lit. If he is looking for the Hall, he shall see us.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: And I will bring up a flask of cocoa. Every watch should have a flask of cocoa.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Light it, Mr Pluck. And let us see who comes home.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Bloom, are all forty pots a different herb? Or have you grown a very large basil by accident?

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: The Terracotta Pots Row. Forty little pots, in a line along the wall, every one with a different herb. It's the most peaceful thing I've ever planted.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: They are lovely, Mark. I think I shall sit here and draw them.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: You, um, can use my stool.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: That is the nicest offer I have had all week. Thank you, my dear.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Please, no drawing of the basil. It is a very vain herb, and it will start posing.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Zephyrine, you have been sitting on that bench for an hour. Who are you waiting for?

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: The Moon Bench. A stone seat, with a crescent carved into the back, under a trellis of jasmine. I have sat on it before. In a dream, I think, in a very small boat.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Blackwood, you speak as though you have been to every place in this Hall already.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: I think I have, Cornelia. But not in the right order. Everything here feels like a memory of something that has not happened yet.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: That is the most unsettling thing I have ever heard you say, Zephyrine. And I once heard you describe a plague.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: It was a very minor plague, Sam. We had it under control by Thursday.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Cornelia, are those lanterns lit by gas, or by something else?

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Hanging Lantern Cluster. Forty paper lanterns, in forty colours, strung across the courtyard between the arches.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: It's the loveliest thing, Miss Wren. It's like being inside a rainbow, only warmer.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: I have always said that a courtyard is just a room with the roof taken off, and the stars put in. Tonight, I see what I meant.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: That's thirty-six wings restored, Cornelia. And eleven to go.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Eleven to go, Mr Pemberton. Then the Deep Vaults, and the Forgotten Wing, and the Founder's Study. I think we shall meet him there.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Let us have some tea first, my dear. A man cannot meet his founder on an empty stomach.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: The Courtyard Orchard Tree! It's got apples, Miss Wren, and pears, and one very confused plum. Grafted all on to the same trunk.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: I did, um, wonder if it would take. It looks happy.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Bloom, you grafted this?

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: The founder left a note about it, in the Herb Jar. It said: Do try the plum. Nobody believes it will work.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: I shall make a tart of all three, and call it The Argument.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: I have just seen a robin in the plum. It is the first time any bird has defended it.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Great Moon Lantern. A silver paper globe, ten feet across, glowing from within, and hung from the centre of the courtyard like a second moon.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: My dears. It is the loveliest thing I have seen. It makes the whole garden look like a dream somebody is having on purpose.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: It's got seventy-two little mirrors inside, and a very good wick. I've never been so pleased with a lantern.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: The first replies have come, Cornelia. Eleven members have written back. Two of them are, I fear, quite rude.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Splendid. A rude reply is a reply nonetheless, and the Society has always run on those. Put them in the Great Index, Miss Quill.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: The Dragonfly Perch! A little brass reed in a stone basin, and, perching on it, a dragonfly with wings like stained glass.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Do you know, Zephyrine, that is the oldest insect in the Hall? It is more than three hundred million years old.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: Then it has been watching this Hall for a very long time, Aldous. It must have seen many things.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: I asked it if it had seen the founder.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: And what did it say, Barnaby?

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: It said nothing. It just flew in a little circle, and landed on my nose. I think that means yes.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: The Koi Pond Rim! A carp as long as my arm, gold and white, with a mouth like a very polite door.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: I've named him Gerald, Miss Bose. He likes bread.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Gerald shall not have bread. He shall have a small cup of peas, as the Society's physician advises.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: I have not advised that. I have no idea who has been advising that.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Professor, you advised it yourself last Tuesday. You were looking at a heron at the time, and said yes to everything I asked.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Swan Boat. A white, gilt-trimmed pleasure boat, with two painted swans on the prow. I recall rowing in it once, when I was very small.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: You rowed in it, Cornelia? I did not know you were here as a child.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: I was not. That is, I... I must have been mistaken. It is a very easy thing to confuse a boat with a memory.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Cornelia, you were here as a child. Do not tell me you have forgotten.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: I have not forgotten, Rosalind. I merely have not decided how to say it.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Waterfall Rockery! A little cascade, tumbling over seven steps of moss-green stone, and going round and round on a very discreet little pump.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: It makes a lovely noise, Hugo. It sounds like somebody pouring a very long cup of tea.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: That's the whole point of it, Barnaby. It's the sound of a thing doing exactly what it should, forever.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: The, um, ferns love it. They're doing something I've never seen. They're leaning towards the water, like they're listening.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: Everything leans towards something in this Hall. It is only a question of what.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Great Reflecting Pool Fountain. Nine jets of water, rising and falling in the shape of a flower, in a basin so still that it holds the sky.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: It is the most beautiful thing, my dears. I have no wish to speak.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: A carriage has stopped at the gate, Cornelia. A very expensive carriage, with a very expensive horse, and a crest of golden scales.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Gilded League. They have sent a man.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Lucian Merrick. We were friends once, in the sense that two crows are friends. He is the most charming, and the least honest, man alive. I'd say he has come to make you an offer.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Then he shall have his tea, Mr Vane. And we shall see how charming he is when it is cold.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Heating Pipe Coil. A great brass snake of piping, running along the floor, hot to the touch. It's what keeps the whole Glasshouse tropical.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: Thank you, Hugo. The palms have been, um, shivering for twenty years.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: It was no trouble. It's all a matter of getting the water to the right temperature, and keeping it there. Same as a good cup of tea.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: It is a much easier thing to keep a pipe warm than a person, Hugo.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Anjali, was that a compliment, or a criticism?

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: Hugo, I do not know. I have not decided. Drink your tea.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: The Chameleon Branch! Miss Wren, I've been looking at it for ten minutes, and I can't find the chameleon.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: It is quite difficult to find a chameleon, Mr Pluck. That is the whole purpose of one.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: He's on your sleeve, Barnaby. Left cuff.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Oh! So he is. He's gone the colour of my cuff. It's the same colour as the gravy.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Splendid! He has chosen your coat as the safest place in the Menagerie. It is a high compliment.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: The Aquarium Corner! A tank of little striped fish, half hidden among the weeds. I think I have seen these before, in the Great Aquarium.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: They're the descendants, Professor. Of the fish in the Aquarium. They, um, swam through a pipe I did not know about.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: A pipe? Show me. I'll bet it's the same pipe that appears on the Gasworks Model.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: I did not think to look.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: A pipe from the Great Aquarium to the Menagerie, and on, I suspect, to the Deep Vaults. The Hall is a great deal more connected than the plans allow.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: The Mist Sprayer! A fine brass nozzle, a little pipe, and a fog as soft as breath. All the ferns are drinking it in, and the whole room looks like a morning.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: I should like to paint it. Look, the light is coming through, and it is golden.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: The sprayer was the first thing I fixed when I came here. I did it, um, before I even said hello.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Bloom, I did wonder who had been misting the ferns before you arrived.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: I... I think it was me. I think I came here at night, before the Hall was open, and I do not remember doing it.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: It is that sort of building, Mark. Do not trouble yourself. It is a sign that you belong.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: The Stick Insect Frame! A twig, and a twig, and a twig with a very small pair of eyes. Splendid!

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: It's the best hider in the Hall, Professor. I've been looking at it all day.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: It is a very honest creature, Barnaby. It never claims to be anything it is not. It merely lets you assume.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: An enviable talent. I have built a career on it.

lines.speaker: prudence
lines.text: I would have said it was not a talent, Sam, but a lack of ambition.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Prudence, you wound me. I assume you mean it kindly.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Penguin Slide! A little chute of white marble, ending in a pool of green water. Look at them go!

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: They're really sliding, Hugo! One, two, three, splash!

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: It's all in the pitch of the slope, Barnaby. Twenty-two degrees, and a little bit of butter.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Butter, Mr Pemberton?

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Only a very little, Cornelia. For the penguins. It's a tradition.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: I have been looking for my butter all morning. Hugo, I should like to have a word.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: The Giant Tortoise Shell! Methuselah's cousin, I believe. It was brought back from an island in the south, a hundred and eighty years ago. I knew her.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: You knew a tortoise, Miss Blackwood?

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: Her name was Gertrude. She was tremendously dignified, and she ate a hat of mine on a Tuesday. I never forgave her, and I never forgot her.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: I cannot decide whether I wish I had met her, or whether I am glad I did not.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: Both, Rosalind. It is the only honest response.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: The Giant Anteater Corner! He's got a long nose, and a longer tail, and a very polite sort of look about him.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: The giant anteater has a tongue sixty centimetres long, Barnaby. It can flick in and out of a nest a hundred and fifty times a minute.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Can I see?

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: You may not, Barnaby. He is stuffed.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Oh. That's why he hasn't moved all day.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: One would hope so, my boy. Otherwise, I have been giving a very long lecture to a very bored specimen.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: The Glasshouse Weather Cock! A copper rooster on a spindle, spinning in the draught. He tells you which way the wind is blowing, and he's very proud of himself.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Mr Pemberton, which way is the wind blowing?

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: East-north-east, Cornelia. It's a good wind, steady and a little bit damp. I'd say we're in for a fine week.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: That is a very precise prediction, Hugo. I should like to see it written down.

lines.speaker: hugo
lines.text: Professor, I do not write down the weather. I only tell it to the chickens.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: The Menagerie's Prize Beast. A great, glossy, dappled creature of no species I can name, curled in its nest of ferns.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: It is a Golden Okapi, Cornelia! I thought they were extinct. It is a magnificent specimen, and a very good sleeper.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: I have been feeding it ferns since the morning. It is, um, rather affectionate.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: A footman from the League has called. He brought a card, and a hamper, and a very large cheque.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Tell him that the Prize Beast is not for sale, Mr Vane. Neither is the Hall, nor the ferns, nor the okapi's affection.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: With the greatest pleasure, Cornelia. I have wanted to say no to Lucian Merrick for twenty years.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: The Pale Primrose Bed. A drift of silvery flowers that open only after dark. A very modest sort of bloom, and a very grateful one.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.text: I planted them in the afternoon, and they opened at dusk. I've never seen anything so, um, punctual.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: They are rather like the Society, Mark. Quiet, a little shy, and very much in need of an evening.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Miss Thorne, may I borrow your sketchbook? I would like to draw one.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: My dear Barnaby, you may borrow the whole box. And I shall give you your first lesson. Draw what you see, and then draw what you feel.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: The Lantern Vine! A climbing creeper, hung with little glowing berries. They shine green in the dark, and each one is a tiny lamp.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: I know this plant. It grows on the very edge of the known world, in a valley I visited once, and was not allowed to leave.

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: I was there too, Aldous. We have never discussed it.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: No. We have not. I thought it would be indelicate.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: Miss Blackwood, Professor. Was Ambrose Hall with you in that valley?

lines.speaker: zephyrine
lines.text: He was, Cornelia. He walked out of it alone. That was the last time I saw him.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: The Moon Gate Garden. A round stone doorway in a high wall, framing a little courtyard full of jasmine and pale roses.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: I would like to eat my supper here, every night of my life.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: You would eat your supper anywhere, Anjali. You would eat it on a church roof.

lines.speaker: anjali
lines.text: I have. It was delicious. It was a very large church, and the roof was very flat.

lines.speaker: cornelia
lines.text: It is a garden that wishes to be looked at through a hole, Mr Vane. Look at it.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: I am looking, Cornelia. I find that I am rather moved.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: The Great Moon Garden Fountain! A tall stone basin, rimmed with pale flowers, and the water is rising into the air in silver threads.
